pages.name: ACT 1 — The Job: Wake Up Call / Off and Running (p.8–10)

text.content:
The hook. A Fixer (e.g. Diablo) puts the team in front of a Johnson working — deniably — for Ludivenko. The job pays well and sounds simple: make simstar Euphoria vanish for a while, before her first public appearance promoting Strice Foods' Amber Gel. It's a snatch-and-hold, not a hit; the client wants her embarrassed and off the schedule, not hurt.

GM notes. Don't reveal Ludivenko or the Amber Gel angle yet. Let the team do the legwork to case Euphoria — reclusive, guarded, and at Pacific Towers / her studio. This is a straightforward run whose whole point is the later twist: everything the team learns about Euphoria here pays off when they're hired to find her in Act 2.

pages.name: ACT 1 — To Catch A Star / Holding Euphoria / Payday (p.13–24)

text.content:
The grab. Pacific Towers and the surrounding scenes let the team scout and then take Euphoria (To Catch A Star). She is arrogant and uncooperative but not a fighter (see her stat block). The team holds her (Holding Euphoria) until the client's window passes, then hands her back and collects (Payday). Ludivenko gets its sabotaged launch; the runners get paid and move on.

GM notes. Keep it clean — the tone here is a caper, in deliberate contrast to the horror of Act 2. Note who the team is and how they operate; Ludivenko later sells that description to MegaMedia. Map: Pacific Towers.

The wake-up. Run it like the opening call, to the same player. The team celebrated their Act 1 money at a bar run by Clockwork (orange spiked hair, a medallion with a tiny vidscreen looping an old ultraviolent film, a Beethoven fan) on something called Rippers. They wake with brutal hangovers in his storage room to a wristphone chirping in the dark.

The call. Ellery Whitecastle (smoking jacket, fidgeting with a pipe) is nervous: MegaMedia has learned, through street contacts, that he and the team pulled Euphoria's first disappearance. So far they are being civil. They want the team to meet Robert Carrone, her manager, at the Pacific Towers lobby at eleven this morning, and they might forgive the whole thing if the team brings information about their former employers. He'll be in touch. Then Clockwork switches on the lights and shows them out the back door of the storeroom.

Behind the scenes. Euphoria has vanished again, and MegaMedia is leaning on Whitecastle hard: it thinks the runners may know who took her this time. Carrone has the job of getting her back and has chosen, for now, to deal with the runners on reasonable terms; he spoke with Euphoria after the first kidnapping and knows they treated her well. The press does not yet know she is missing.

If they don't show. Whitecastle calls again, urgently. If they still refuse, Carrone sends MegaMedia's Knight Errant guards to collect them, by force if needed. When it's time, go to Meeting Carrone.

Soundboard: QE Soundboard — Act 2: Deja Vu.

The meet. The Pacific Towers guard waves them through and points to the bar, where a tall, lanky redhead in a grey suit (sunglasses pushed up on a hawkish nose) broods over a drink. He offers drinks, then leads them into a small side meeting room, locks the door and switches on a white noise generator.

What Carrone says (MegaMedia VP, her manager for years before that, so it's personal): last weekend's kidnapping cost Euphoria a lucrative Strice Foods deal; another big corporation (he won't say which) has now signed her for a new campaign, and she has vanished again, taken from her condo. If she isn't back by the weekend, that contract is void too. He makes it plain MegaMedia knows the team did the first job; their corporate employer has settled up, and so has Whitecastle — he checks his watch and corrects himself: as did your late friend. Find her and the slate is clean.

The deal. 20,000¥ each, or half if she comes back later than 6 A.M. Saturday (the recording deadline for the new ads). Negotiate as normal: each net success moves it by 1,000¥. He insists on total secrecy (no press, or the sponsor walks) and on full progress reports every eight hours, no exceptions. MegaMedia will explain away the dead Knight Errant guards. His thumbprint opens the lobby elevator to her floor; he takes them up. Go to Missing Again.

Behind the scenes. The new client is Ludivenko (Blue Bacosoy promotions). MegaMedia found out Ludivenko was behind the first job but traded revenge for this contract; Ludivenko handed over Whitecastle's and the runners' names. Carrone had Whitecastle interrogated and killed when it was clear he knew nothing. The runners know nothing about the second abduction either, but while Carrone thinks they might, he wants them working. When they're back on the street, they hear Whitecastle died in a firebomb at his home, identified by dental records.

If they refuse or attack Carrone, they face corporate vengeance; the book suggests ways back into the plot (Euphoria escapes with too much knowledge, someone they know is taken as a host, they witness a snatch or become the target).

Soundboard: QE Soundboard — Act 2: Meeting Carrone.

Arrival. The elevator opens on the 21st-floor hallway. The condo door is ajar; a chair and a cup of cold soykaf sit abandoned at the guard post. Everything is very quiet. In the living room, what's left of several Knight Errant guards — shredded, not shot. Map: Euphoria's Condo (area numbers as in To Catch A Star, p.17).

What happened. After her Monday release, Euphoria and Carrone tried to squeeze Burroughs for money anyway and failed (her contract let him withhold pay). On Tuesday a corporate spy told Burroughs about the Ludivenko deal; he told Craft to get rid of her before she could do it. Craft, dreaming of a Queen, agreed. Tuesday after dark, Soldiers carried Craft and a Worker up the outside of the tower, tore through the greenhouse balcony and made short work of the guards. Euphoria fainted; they carried her and Craft out.

Scene of the crime (p.31):

  • Entrance Hall (1). The abandoned guard post; the main door is open.
  • Living Room (3). All doors open. A large dark stain by the foyer, with shreds of a Knight Errant uniform and an HK227 with a full clip (the front guard never fired). Two more guards' remains. A knowledgeable look: every wound is shredding or tearing, no bullets or blades, and whatever did it was enormously strong. Balcony doors shattered, wind whistling in. Perception (8): large holes in the ceiling running from the balcony to right above the bloodstain. Perception (5): a lump of brown slime near the couch (the Worker drooled raw hive food); anyone who has tasted Amber Gel may link it — Perception (6) by smell, (4) by taste.
  • Recording Studio (4). The gear is still switched on. Replaying needs Electronics (3) or Intelligence (9). Headsets hang on the wall, or a datajack can plug straight in. Go to Private Screening.
  • Greenhouse Balcony (5). Freezing, through a big hole in the plastic shell. The front guard's body is hidden among the tropical plants.

Private Screening (p.32–33). Euphoria was rehearsing Jungle Huntress lines on her wireless Sense Link when they came, so the rig recorded everything. Her deck runs with the inhibitors and filters cut (like a BTL player), at full sensitivity, one generation from the original: whoever plays it lives her raw terror, amplified. Tell the player they can stop at any time (switch off, jack out, rip the headset off). Onlookers see the viewer physically re-enact it, walking out of the studio into the living room.

The two clues in it: the blond, unkempt man who seizes her says Burroughs told him to take care of her, and that he'll make her his Queen; the silent man behind him wears a "Garrety's Bar and Grill" shirt and has something wrong with his eyes. Also: the sickly sweet smell, the clicking not-human laughter, and the one-armed guard who gets a shot off before something drops on him from above.

Handling the chip. Reinstalling the inhibitors: Electronics B/R (4), base time four hours, with tools; after that it's safe. It plays only on her machine unless copied to a simsense or master chip: Electronics (5), base 30 minutes (she has spare chips).

Carrone answers questions without hurting MegaMedia. He knows Burroughs as a Strice Foods executive (they arranged her Amber Gel appearances) and can point them to his office, tenth floor of Soykyo Office Plaza. He does not recognize Craft from the recording.

Next. Magic can't find her (the Queen shrouds her astral form). Legwork p.56; a decker into Strice Foods: Hacking Strice p.34; Garrety's Bar and Grill: Missing Persons p.35; Burroughs: Hey, Vince! p.36. If they miss the recording, Carrone finds it later and tells them they should experience it.

Soundboard: QE Soundboard — Act 2: Missing Again (the full Private Screening playback is one clip).

Where Euphoria is actually being held in the early adventure — a cheap rented flat at Royal Meadows, supplied by Ludivenko. This location has a printed floorplan and, until this revision, had no scene in the module at all.

Play it cramped. The flat is 8 × 3 metres — 24 m² for a living room/kitchenette, a bedroom with two double beds squeezed side by side, a closet and a bathroom. That is not a mistake in the map: the book says these units are packed with people and that the owners have accommodated the overcrowding by adding more beds. There is nowhere to take cover and nowhere to flank.

What a search turns up. The cupboards hold sealed dehydrated food, courtesy of Ludivenko. The dresser drawers and the closet hold women's clothing in average size, still in plastic wrap — bought for Euphoria, not by her. That detail alone tells the runners someone is keeping her here rather than hiding with her.

Texture for the squalor: one of the two chairs will break if anyone sits on it, the refrigerator's freezer does not work, the sink's water filters are disgusting, the living-room ceiling air filter badly needs changing, and the bathroom's hot water faucet does not work.

If the runners annoy the building manager, about 100¥ calms him down.

Map: Royal Meadows — Flat.

Legwork around Strice Foods, Ludivenko, and MegaMedia fills in the corporate triangle behind both abductions. Key names:

  • Vincent Burroughs — the Strice Foods exec who secretly buys Craft's substance to make Amber Gel, and who tells Craft to "take care of" Euphoria (a social contact / journal dossier, not a combatant).
  • Solomon Daniels — Craft's Fixer, who offered him the run that restarted his shadow career.
  • Osprey and Stone — Euphoria's own protection, not Craft's: Osprey is her MegaMedia bodyguard and commands the Knight Errant detail at her condo, and Stone is the street mage he brought in for magical protection (p.17, p.20–21). They are Act 1 opposition; their stat blocks are in the Cast compendium.
  • Ludivenko / Strice / MegaMedia — the corps; Ludivenko is the hidden hand behind Act 1.

Rewards funnel. The paydata trail (see Hacking Strice) links Amber Gel to a mysterious supplier and to Craft's talismonger shop, Magic Crafts — the door to the Hive.

If the team decks Strice Foods, run it against the Strice Foods Host actor (see the Cast compendium) and its IC. The system holds no vital clue, but it is profitable and it ties Amber Gel to Craft: purchase-order records (DS-1) show the plant receives only jars, blue coloring, and low-grade nutrisoy — no way to make a stuffer from that alone — plus the MegaMedia payment (1,280,000¥ for Euphoria's three appearances) and Knight Errant security expenditures. A rent memo or payment can point at Magic Crafts and Craft.

Paydata: DS-1 4×70 Mp (~28,000¥), DS-2 3×80 Mp (~60,000¥), DS-3 2×40 Mp (~4,000¥). Trap: an external alert shuts the whole system down within two minutes; a Trace prints at Burroughs' terminal and he calls Lone Star. Per-node Security Codes and TNs are documented on the host actor's notes.

Craft's talismonger shop. The trail leads here. Craft appears (when present) as a filthy, unkempt man reeking of regurgitation, his behavior swinging between the affable merchant and the Ant-crazed shaman. The shop is a front and a bolthole; astral traces, ritual materials, and the smell of the Hive are all present to a careful investigator.

GM notes. Craft is a dangerous full magician (Sorcery 6 / Conjuring 5, Ant totem) — see his stat block. Do not let the team corner him easily; he would rather flee to the Hive with his prize than fight to the death in his shop. Map: Craft's Magic Shop — Upper Level.

A MegaMedia studio scene — pressure from the corp, a public-appearance angle, or a staged event tied to the Amber Gel promotion. Use it to raise the stakes and the clock, and to give social characters room to work. Map: MegaMedia — Simsense Studio.

pages.name: Audience With The Queen — The Hive (p.43–52)

text.content:
The climax. The team descends into Craft's Hive to free Euphoria before her metamorphosis completes. It is a nest of chambers, cocoons, and larvae, defended by Soldier and Worker ant spirits (true and flesh forms — see the Insect Spirits primer and the Cast compendium). Craft is here, at the height of his madness, summoning his Queen.

Euphoria is cocooned and mid-metamorphosis; every round of delay is a round closer to losing her. Freeing her is a matter of cutting her loose and getting out — through the Hive's defenders.

GM notes. Workers scream to summon Soldiers and throw themselves at attackers near the cocoons or the Queen. Read the Insect Spirits primer first — it was rewritten from the printed tables and three rules this module previously used were wrong (there is no Immunity to Normal Weapons, armour is Force × 1 and only on True Forms, and melee uses ordinary skill).

Maps: The Hive — Main Level (p.44) then The Hive — Lower Level (p.45). The Lower Level is dark: neither light nor power, and every internal wall is Barrier Rating 3 — the book says Soldiers making an all-out attack will use the thin walls to their advantage, so let them come through walls.

Printed occupants of the Lower Level — place these rather than improvising:

  • Room 1 — the elevator arrives here. Empty unless the Hive has been alerted.
  • Room 3 — six Flesh Form Workers (F1), two Flesh Form Soldiers (F3).
  • Room 8 — the stairway exits here. Two Flesh Form Workers (F1).
  • Room 14 — four Flesh Form Workers (F1), two Flesh Form Soldiers (F3).
  • Room 15 — five Flesh Form Workers (F1) and a lone Flesh Form Soldier (Force 5).
  • Room 16 — the Hive Room. The climax.
  • Rooms 2, 4–7 and 9–13 are as Room 1.
